edition.title: Morning paper, Monday 19 October 2026
edition.fact: Edition 14. Anchor day for India's largest IPO; Saturday's banks face their first vote. Monday 19 October 2026: the Nifty 50 closed Friday at 23,146.15, up 2.78% on the week. Jio Platforms' anchor book opens today, four IPOs close today, and markets are shut tomorrow for Dussehra. The long read is Zoho.
edition.intro: The lead route below takes about 5 minutes. Sections after it carry the detail. Today the anchor book of India's largest-ever IPO decides who gets in early, while the stock market gives its first verdict on Saturday's bank results after a day to digest them.

concept.label: One concept a day
concept.name: The grey market premium
concept.line: What an IPO's unofficial premium actually measures - the mood of a small speculative crowd, not the value of the company. Unregulated, thin, and often wrong on listing day.

blocks.html: Jio anchor day: institutions bid today for the roughly ₹8,000 crore anchor book of Jio Platforms' ₹30,213 crore IPO (band ₹1,065 to ₹1,119). Mint reports nearly ₹2.5 lakh crore of indicated interest. The issue opens Wednesday.

Banks' first vote: ICICI Bank beat estimates, HDFC Bank was in line with a narrower margin, and Axis Bank's headline growth hid a profit miss; today is the first trading session since the results. IDBI Bank's 39% profit fall flips to a 14% rise once a one-off is excluded.

Insurance: banks are counting the cost of IRDAI's proposed commission caps: RBL Bank estimates a 50 to 60% hit to bancassurance income and Canara Bank up to ₹200 crore. Comments on the draft close Sunday 25 October.
Economy: the Cabinet cleared the sale of 60.72% of IDBI Bank to Fairfax for ₹52,878 crore, and the finance minister blamed excess liquidity and easy exits for the market's 12% slide this year.
AI: Meta's Muse Wonder and Google's Gemini 4 Argon now have independent scorecards: Artificial Analysis ranks both just behind the frontier leaders. Argon's introductory price doubles on 30 November.
Markets: the Nifty's recovery week was led by IT, up 11.72% on NSE data; resistance sits at 23,300 to 23,350. US inflation worsened to 3.7% in September.
Long read: Zoho never raised a rupee of venture money, crossed ₹12,313 crore of revenue, and is now freezing pay as AI squeezes software economics.

groups.heading: Editor's read: Monday answers two questions by 3:30 pm

blocks.html: The first question is what Saturday's bank results are worth. My read: ICICI Bank gains and leads the private-bank pack today, HDFC Bank sags as the market works through its 3.16% margin, and the Bank Nifty underperforms the Nifty 50 on the day. The numbers support a split verdict, not a uniform rally: the best quarter (ICICI's) was genuinely strong, the biggest bank's was thin underneath, and Axis's 37.6% profit jump still landed below what the street had pencilled in. My confidence: moderate. What would prove me wrong by the close: HDFC Bank finishing more than 1% higher, or the Bank Nifty beating the Nifty 50. The second question is whether Jio's anchor book confirms the reported demand. If the book fills with the sovereign funds named in the reporting (ADIA, QIA, GIC, Norges, Mubadala, BlackRock), expect the grey market premium, ₹235 on Sunday, to hold into Wednesday's open; a book that fills mostly with domestic mutual funds instead would say global money balked at the price. Note the counterweight underneath the excitement: Jio's revenue per user has barely moved, ₹215.6 a month at the end of March from ₹214 the previous quarter, and the IPO asks ₹10.3 lakh crore for the company anyway.
Source: CNBC-TV18 stocks to watch / Mint anchor book / Mint GMP and interest

blocks.title: Jio's anchor day: a reported ₹2.5 lakh crore of interest for an ₹8,000 crore book

blocks.html: Anchor investors place their bids today for Jio Platforms, India's largest public issue ever: up to 27 crore fresh shares at ₹1,065 to ₹1,119 apiece, raising up to ₹30,213 crore and valuing the company at about ₹10.3 lakh crore at the top of the band. The anchor book is roughly ₹8,000 crore; Mint reports indicated interest of nearly ₹2.5 lakh crore across sovereign funds (ADIA, QIA, GIC, Norges, Mubadala), asset managers (BlackRock, Fidelity, the Goldman Sachs and Franklin Templeton arms), LIC and about 15 domestic mutual funds. By rule, up to 60% of the QIB portion can go to anchors, and half of the anchor portion is reserved for domestic mutual funds. There is no offer-for-sale: Meta, Google, KKR, Silver Lake and General Atlantic all stay put, and the money goes to the company, mostly to prepay up to ₹27,500 crore of Reliance Jio Infocomm's borrowings.

Two sweeteners widen the tent: a reservation of up to ₹2,500 crore for anyone who held Reliance Industries shares as of 14 October, and ₹500 crore for employees at a ₹54 discount. Retail's minimum ticket is 12 shares, ₹13,428 at the top of the band. The grey market premium stood at about ₹235 on Sunday, roughly 21% over the cap price, after climbing from ₹148 on 4 October (unofficial tracker data). Uday Kotak, whose bank leads the issue, said the band was "priced for investors to have returns in this IPO." The fundamental question underneath: monthly revenue per user has gone from ₹214 to ₹215.6 in two quarters, and managing director Akash Ambani is asking investors to price the upside from services beyond licensed telecom, naming voice AI as an example. Allotment is due 26 October, listing 28 October.
The grey market premium climbed 50% in two weeks into the anchor book. Unofficial, unregulated, and often wrong on listing day; treat it as sentiment, not price discovery.
Source: ET IPO week / Mint anchor book / Mint GMP + interest

blocks.title: The Saturday banks get their Monday vote

blocks.html: Friday's close gave investors their last look at bank prices before the first big results weekend of the season; today they get to act. What they are pricing: ICICI Bank's standalone profit rose 20.1% to ₹14,843 crore with interest income up 17.7% to ₹25,339 crore, both ahead of estimates, and asset quality improved. HDFC Bank's ₹19,510 crore, up 4.7%, was in line, but the margin on its lending narrowed to 3.16% and treasury income fell 67.4%; interest income grew 9.7%. Axis Bank's profit jumped 37.6% to ₹7,003 crore, helped by a low base, yet still missed what analysts expected, even as interest income of ₹15,372 crore beat; gross bad loans fell to 1.16% of the book. The quarter's trap for headline readers is IDBI Bank: profit fell 39% to about ₹2,205 crore, but excluding the year-ago one-off gain from selling its NSDL stake, profit actually rose 14%, with interest income up 28.7% and margin at 4.11%. Yes Bank's profit rose 65% to ₹1,080 crore and Central Bank of India's rose 21.1% to ₹1,469 crore, with the latter's board approving up to ₹7,000 crore of bond fundraising.

Context for the vote: bank stocks lagged the rally last week (the Nifty Private Bank index rose 1.76% against the Nifty's 2.78%), so results were not priced for perfection. Today's results calendar adds Bajaj Finance, UltraTech Cement, Hindustan Zinc and Union Bank of India. The rest of the season is compressed by Tuesday's Dussehra holiday: Infosys, JSW Steel, Tata Motors, Dr Reddy's, IndusInd Bank and Coforge report Friday; Kotak Mahindra Bank, AU Small Finance Bank and IDFC First Bank on Saturday.
Source: CNBC-TV18 stocks to watch / BusinessToday week ahead

blocks.title: IRDAI's commission caps land on bank earnings calls

blocks.html: The regulator's draft cap on insurance commissions stopped being an industry story over the weekend and became a bank-earnings story. RBL Bank estimates its bancassurance income could fall 50 to 60% if the proposals pass as drafted; Canara Bank puts the hit to distribution income at up to ₹200 crore, of which ₹120 to 145 crore is from life insurance. The large private banks are more sanguine: ICICI Bank says third-party products are under 1% of its total income; HDFC Bank's CFO called the commission cuts "quite high" but pointed to possible offsetting gains from better persistency and volumes; Axis Bank says it will chase volumes, product mix and a bigger share of partners' business. IIFL Capital sizes the industry's bancassurance income pool at about $2.2 billion after three years of 28% annual growth, contributing nearly 10% of banks' fee income and about 3% of sector profits, with the contribution highest at Axis, HDFC and Kotak. The draft proposes separate, higher caps for individual distributors than for corporate ones, on the logic that a person spends more effort selling than a bank branch does. Banks are preparing their feedback now; comments close Sunday 25 October.
Source: Business Standard / BS on transition

blocks.title: The finance minister's diagnosis: too much liquidity, too many easy exits

blocks.html: Speaking to CNBC on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank meetings in Bangkok, Nirmala Sitharaman blamed India's 12% equity-market slide this year partly on the market itself: "Because of the ease of liquidity, ease of availability, people are even exiting easily." She called capital outflows one of India's biggest risks for 2027 (foreign investors have sold over $33 billion of Indian equities this year, per NSDL), and argued India would not be "hurt" if the global AI bubble bursts because the AI money never came here. The data behind the underperformance claim is stark: Taiwan and Korea now hold 29% and 22% of the MSCI Asia Pacific ex-Japan index while India's weight has compressed from 19% to 10% (Goldman Sachs), and 63% of the $60.4 billion raised in Indian IPOs from 2021 to 2025 went to selling shareholders rather than to companies (EY). Against that: domestic mutual funds have taken net inflows every month since March 2021, and domestic institutions absorbed most of last week's foreign selling. Separately, the Cabinet cleared the biggest financial-sector FDI India has done: Fairfax Financial takes 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore, targeted to close this financial year.
Source: CNBC interview / Mint on IDBI

groups.heading: Insurance: the week the feedback lands

blocks.title: Six days to comment: what the industry is telling IRDAI

blocks.html: Feedback on the distribution-reform draft closes Sunday 25 October. The fault lines are now visible. Agents, through their federation LIAFI, are asking for the opposite of caps: first-year commissions up to 35% on long-term life policies. Banks, the largest corporate distributors, are modelling income hits and preparing responses (see Front page). The regulator's public line, from IRDAI chairman Ajay Seth, is that the reforms aim for an "orderly transition", not disruption. For anyone working in distribution, the practical calendar is: responses this week, final regulations after, and the proposed structure (product- and channel-specific commission caps, tighter expense-of-management limits, separate and higher caps for individual agents versus corporate distributors) as the negotiating baseline. The draft's consumer-facing half, a ban on dark patterns on insurance websites and no phone-number collection before a price is shown, has attracted less pushback and is the part most likely to survive close to its drafted form.
Source: Business Standard / BS on Ajay Seth

groups.heading: AI: the agent models get independent scorecards

blocks.title: Muse Wonder: Meta's agents impress a third party, but the best version is paywalled inside Meta's own tool

blocks.html: Meta's Muse Wonder pair, announced 12 October, is its first serious bid for agent work: models that keep context across conversations (Active Memory) and pursue a goal through errors while asking before consequential actions (Active Focus). The independent check exists this time: benchmarking firm Artificial Analysis scores Muse Wonder Full at 56 on its Intelligence Index, tied with Claude Sonnet 5.5 and behind only Claude Opus 5.5 at 58; the standard Wonder scores 52, one point behind GPT-6 Astra and Gemini 4 Argon at 53. Meta's own table also shows the models do not lead everywhere: Opus 5.5 and Astra beat Wonder Full on Terminal-Bench, and Opus leads on health questions. The catches are commercial, not technical. The stronger Full version has no API price at all; it lives inside Meta's Muse Code subscriptions at $50 and $200 a month. Neither model offers downloadable weights. And Muse Code defaults to Contributor mode, which lets Meta train on what you submit unless you switch it off; the pay-as-you-go API runs in Standard mode, which Meta says does not train on your data. API price for the standard model: $4 per million input tokens, $20 per million output.
Source: VentureBeat / eesel review

blocks.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Google's long-task model, with a price that doubles on 30 November

blocks.html: Google's 13 October launch targets multi-step work in coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity and science, with a one-million-token window. Google's claims that it ranks first on the Vals Index and scores 87% on the ERQA embodied-reasoning benchmark are vendor-reported; the independent anchor is the same Artificial Analysis index, where Argon scores 53, level with GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1, behind Claude Opus 5.5 and Muse Wonder Full. What would verify the vendor claims: broader third-party evaluations beyond a single composite index, which take a few weeks to accumulate. The practical note is pricing: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output until 30 November, then $4 and $20. Teams evaluating it have six weeks at half price.
Source: Aiholics weekly / VentureBeat

blocks.title: Indian AI money: a ₹3,000 crore growth fund with Nandan Nilekani as anchor

blocks.html: Fundamentum Frontier Advisors raised ₹3,000 crore in subscriptions for a growth-stage AI and deeptech fund, with Nandan Nilekani anchoring and mentoring; the fund plans to write ₹100 to 200 crore cheques into 12 to 15 companies over two to three years. The week's deal flow backed the theme: AI agent startup RapidCanvas raised $29 million from Vertex Ventures, AI video platform Clueso $10 million from Dharana Capital, AI gaming studio Spill Games $10.5 million from Elevation Capital, and seed rounds for Parallel Loop ($6.6 million) and Shamrock AI ($5 million). Overall, 28 Indian startups raised $302.85 million in the week to 17 October, 2.7 times the previous week, led by Tessolve Semiconductor's $75 million round.
Source: Entrackr weekly

groups.heading: Markets: the recovery week, in numbers

blocks.title: An IT-led week, straight from the NSE files

blocks.html: The Nifty 50 rose 2.78% to 23,146.15 last week and the Sensex 3.11% to 74,729.27, a second straight weekly gain after the eight-week slide, the longest in 25 years. The NSE's own index files show how narrow the leadership was: Nifty IT rose 11.72% (its results season, plus what traders are calling the reverse-AI trade as money rotates out of crowded AI names), Media 6.11%, Auto 3.65%. The laggards were Healthcare (-1.08%), Pharma (-0.69%), FMCG (-0.55%) and PSU banks (-0.39%). Foreign investors sold ₹15,440 crore through the week; domestic institutions bought ₹14,792 crore, nearly cancelling it out. The rupee had its own recovery: six straight sessions of gains, up 2% on the week to 94.95 per dollar, the best-performing emerging-market currency, after RBI measures to curb dollar demand. Brent settled at $109.86 a barrel, its highest since May.

blocks.title: The setup for a three-and-a-half-session week

blocks.html: The Nifty sits above its 10- and 20-day averages but below its 50- and 200-day ones; the 23,300 to 23,350 zone, which is both the 50-day average and the top of the 24 September gap down, is the resistance that decides whether this is a recovery or a bounce. Above that, 23,500. Support: 22,900 to 23,000, then 22,800. Options positioning agrees, with the heaviest open interest at the 23,500 call and 22,700 put. India VIX is 14.02, calm but not comfortable. The weekly chart shows a Morning Star-type bullish pattern after two months of decline, per HDFC Securities' technical desk. This week is short: Dussehra shuts the market tomorrow, and Jio's subscription window (Wednesday to Friday) plus a heavy results slate (Infosys, JSW Steel, Tata Motors, Dr Reddy's on Friday; Kotak, AU and IDFC First on Saturday) do the talking. Globally, the mood is the counterweight: US inflation worsened to 3.7% in September and the Nasdaq just had its worst week since June, falling 2% on Friday alone.
Source: Moneycontrol trade setup / CNBC-TV18 stocks to watch

blocks.title: The week's movers, with the reason attached

blocks.html: Tech Mahindra, up 18% for the week: profit grew 32.8% to ₹1,586 crore in the September quarter, the board declared a ₹15 interim dividend and a 1:1 bonus, and Jefferies upgraded the stock. TCS, up 14%, and Infosys, up 12.5%: the same earnings-driven IT rotation, with results anchoring it. Onward Technologies, up 20% on Friday alone (upper circuit): September-quarter profit rose 41.7% to ₹17 crore and revenue 22.4% to ₹170.2 crore, with operating margin expanding a point to 15.6%. Where the reason is not publicly clear, the mover is left out rather than guessed.
Source: BusinessLine on TechM / CNBC-TV18 on Onward / BusinessToday

groups.heading: IPO: four close today, two open Wednesday, nine list this week

blocks.title: Closing today: Tonbo is the retail favourite, Zetwerk the laggard

blocks.html: Subscription status at Friday's close, the last reading before today's final day: Tonbo Imaging 7.77 times (retail 7.12x, non-institutional 14.35x), Sahajanand Medical Technologies 0.82 times, Bonfiglioli Transmissions 0.99 times and Zetwerk 0.31 times. Grey market premiums on Sunday implied listings 72% above the issue price for Tonbo (₹1,205 against ₹700), 22% for Bonfiglioli, 6.4% for Sahajanand and 4.6% for Zetwerk. Zetwerk is the size play of the four (a ₹5,012 crore issue with a ₹2,830 crore fresh component, the rest an offer-for-sale) and it softened last week despite a ₹2,251 crore anchor book that included Capital Group's two arms (about ₹288 crore, 12.88% of the anchor allocation), Prashant Jain's 3P India Equity Fund, BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, Nomura, Société Générale, Manulife and Prudential. Worth a closer look: Tonbo, the defence-optics maker, on retail demand and grey-market signal; what would make that wrong is a cold Friday listing session for the whole cohort, or day-three subscription that fades instead of accelerating as final-day retail piles in. All four list on Friday 23 October.
Source: Mint GMP race / Entrackr on Zetwerk anchors

blocks.title: Wednesday: Paras Healthcare opens alongside Jio

blocks.html: Paras Healthcare's ₹1,450 crore issue (band ₹660 to ₹693, minimum 21 shares, ₹14,553 at the top) combines a ₹500 crore fresh issue with a ₹950 crore offer-for-sale. The chain runs eight hospitals with 2,211 beds across Gurugram, Panchkula, Patna and five other cities, turned a ₹43.83 crore profit in FY26 after a ₹57.98 crore loss in FY25, and plans to add 800 beds by March 2028. Both Paras and Jio close on Friday and are scheduled to list on 28 October. The week's listing queue: HD Fire Protect on Wednesday, Fusion CX on Thursday, and Tonbo, Zetwerk, Bonfiglioli and Sahajanand on Friday.
Source: ET IPO week

blocks.title: JSW Steel gets ₹2,169 crore of Odisha mining demands struck or sent back

blocks.html: The Odisha High Court quashed a ₹696.32 crore demand against JSW Steel for a first-year mineral-dispatch shortfall at its Jajang iron ore block, and set aside a separate ₹1,472.69 crore demand for the fifth year, sending it back to the mining authority for fresh consideration under the legal position the court set out in an April judgment. Both demands were raised under Rule 12-A of the mineral concession rules, which penalises dispatch shortfalls; the judgments were pronounced on 16 October and disclosed by the company on Sunday. For JSW, which reports results on Friday, the timing is convenient: a potential ₹2,169 crore overhang shrinks to one remanded case.
Source: ET on the ruling

blocks.title: Vedanta turns on a $600 million zinc expansion in South Africa

blocks.html: Vedanta has doubled the annual capacity of its Gamsberg mine to 500,000 tonnes of zinc, a $600 million investment inaugurated on Sunday by South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Vedanta director Priya Agarwal-Hebbar. The expansion advances the group's target of 3 million tonnes a year of zinc across India and South Africa (2 million from Hindustan Zinc, 1 million from Vedanta Zinc International) and forms part of the ZAR 21 billion commitment Vedanta made at the 2018 South Africa Investment Conference. The demand case: galvanisation, the coating that keeps steel from corroding, tied to construction and car output.
Source: Business Standard

blocks.title: Groww's CAS quarter: profit up 54%, derivatives revenue down 14%

blocks.html: Groww's parent Billionbrains Garage Ventures reported a 54% rise in quarterly profit to ₹725.6 crore on revenue up 44% to ₹1,541 crore, while equity-derivatives revenue fell 14.3% quarter on quarter, which the company attributes largely to SEBI's closing auction system, live since 3 August. Derivatives now contribute 45% of revenue. Read together with last week's circular pushing the auction to a 3:30-3:40 pm window from 7 December, the exchange-minutes-to-revenue pipeline is now a disclosed, measurable line in a listed broker's numbers.
Source: Moneycontrol / Entrackr

blocks.title: Quick hits: Urban Company's war chest, Nazara's founder steps back, UPI fees wait, Qualcomm exits Shadowfax

items: Urban Company approved raising up to ₹2,500 crore through equity and convertible securities, including a possible QIP, as competition in its InstaHelp quick-services vertical from Snabbit and Pronto intensifies; shareholder and regulatory approvals are still needed.

Nazara Technologies founder Nitish Mittersain will step down as managing director to become founder and non-executive director; Mithun Padam Sacheti becomes executive director and Arun Agrawal joins as CFO.

NPCI deferred the planned 15 October rollout of MDR on select UPI transactions until after Diwali; the September framework charges 0.4% (capped at ₹300) on eligible merchant transactions above ₹2,000.
Qualcomm Ventures sold a further 0.98% of Shadowfax Technologies for ₹157.28 crore, taking its open-market exits to about ₹341 crore across two sales; it held 2.26% at the end of June.

blocks.html: Source: Entrackr weekly

blocks.title: $302.85 million across 28 deals, semiconductors on top

blocks.html: Indian startup funding jumped 2.7 times week on week to $302.85 million across 28 deals in the week to 17 October. Growth-stage deals took $220.37 million: Tessolve Semiconductor's $75 million from Vector Line Capital led, followed by sports brand Boldfit's ₹400 crore Series B from Bharat Value Fund, RapidCanvas's $29 million and Scimplify's $25 million from Hitachi Ventures. Early-stage added $82.48 million across 21 deals, led by Mesa School of Business's ₹110 crore. The pattern to note: five AI deals in a week when the sector's growth capital also found a dedicated ₹3,000 crore vehicle (see AI section). Also on the launch pad: boAt entered Sri Lanka and Bhutan, Swiggy turned on multi-restaurant ordering for the festive season, and CoinSwitch Ventures rebranded to BlackLane Capital with a wider mandate.
Source: Entrackr weekly

blocks.title: One startup idea: the anchor-book analyst for retail

blocks.html: Every large IPO now runs a one-day anchor book that retail investors cannot see until the allotment disclosure lands. A product that tracks anchor allocations across issues (who bid, at what cut-off, how the same funds' past anchor allocations performed to listing and to 90 days) would give retail applicants a real signal to replace the grey market premium. The data is public but scattered across exchange filings; the moat is a clean historical dataset. The risk: anchors are a noisy signal, as Zetwerk's star-studded book and 31% subscription this week show.
Source: Mint anchor book

groups.heading: Global: the inflation print behind the tech wobble

blocks.title: US inflation worsens to 3.7%, and the Nasdaq has its worst week since June

blocks.html: US consumer prices rose 3.7% in September, up from 3.4% in August and above expectations, reviving talk that the Federal Reserve's next move could be a hike rather than a cut. The stock market's response has been to sell the most crowded trade: the Nasdaq fell 2% on Friday to complete its worst week since June, dragged by technology and AI-linked names. The connection to Indian screens is direct: the same inflation print is part of why money rotated into Indian IT last week (the "reverse AI trade" in trader shorthand), and part of why foreign investors kept selling Indian equities even as the Nifty rose. For the week ahead, watch whether US yields keep climbing; if they do, the FII selling that domestic institutions have been absorbing is unlikely to stop.
Source: AP on CPI / AP on markets

groups.heading: One Concept a Day: the grey market premium

blocks.html: When you read that Jio's grey market premium is ₹235, you are reading the price of a promise. Before an IPO lists, small operators run an unofficial market where people agree to buy or sell their not-yet-allotted shares at a fixed premium over the issue price. If you are allotted shares at ₹1,119 and sell your allotment in the grey market at a ₹235 premium, the buyer pays you the premium now and the trade settles informally after listing, whatever the market price then is. Three things to hold about the number. First, it is unregulated and off-exchange: no clearing house, no guarantee, no SEBI oversight, just word and WhatsApp. Second, it is thin: a few hundred crores of informal interest can move the quoted premium, so it measures the mood of a small speculative crowd, not the value of the company. Third, it has a memory: premiums routinely collapse on listing day when the wider market gets its first real vote, and an IPO can list below its grey-implied price even after weeks of strong premiums. Use it the way this paper does: as a sentiment gauge with a date on it, never as a price target.
